title: UK households could save over £370 a year by repairing instead of replacing | Klarna International
body_markdown:
**London, 29th September 2026** — Klarna, the everyday finance network, is launching Care & Repair in the UK and France, a new feature that makes it easier for shoppers to repair, alter and care for the clothing and shoes they already own, rather than replace them. Built in partnership with Save Your Wardrobe, the aftersales platform powering post-purchase infrastructure for global brands and retailers, Care & Repair helps shoppers save in just a few taps, with repair and alteration options visible on past purchases in the Klarna app.


Just 14% of UK shoppers have ever used a brand's repair service despite 70% knowing that repairing can save them money, according to new research from a joint report by Klarna, Save Your Wardrobe, and sustainability consultancy Create Sustain.


The average British household could save as much as £370* a year by repairing instead of replacing, but adoption is low because most don't know repair services exist or don't know where to access them. Klarna's Care & Repair feature will help close this gap by making repairs easy and affordable.


**The smarter way to shop**


For UK consumers, the main benefit to repairing is saving money: 69% say they'd be more likely to buy a product if a retailer offered free repairs for its lifetime. Beyond the direct saving, 73% say repair helps them get better value from what they already own, and knowing that repair is available changes how people shop in the first place: 68% say it would make them more willing to invest in a higher-quality item.


This matters because the value equation is tight for most shoppers: almost 3 in 5 UK consumers typically spend less than £50 on something they intend to keep long term. For repair to make financial sense at that price point, it has to be simple, fairly priced and easy to find, which is exactly what Care & Repair addresses by making repairs simpler and more affordable. Price is the single biggest thing UK consumers say would encourage them to repair more (38%), ahead of any other factor.


**Removing the biggest barrier: access**


While affordability is the top reason UK consumers give for not repairing more (35%), the more fixable problem is discoverability. Only 42% of UK shoppers know that brands offer repair services at all. A quarter (25%) say they simply don't know where to go.


"This is a gap in access and awareness, not appetite. 77% of UK consumers want brands to make their repair services more visible, and demand for a genuinely easy experience is consistent across the data, from faster turnaround, to easier booking and drop-off, to home collection options. Care & Repair addresses this directly by sitting inside a step shoppers already take, checking their past purchases, rather than asking them to go looking for a repair service on their own. We want to make repairing as easy as buying new", explains


**Louisa Garcia Moreno, Sustainability Communications Lead, Klarna** .


*Read more in the full Repair Culture in Fashion report*[here](https://locker.klarna.com/asset/a6f00168-a883-400e-8486-7d61dd0b7fdf/Web_RepairCultureInFashion_Document_16x9_en.pdf)


*.*


**How Care & Repair works**


Care & Repair is built directly into the Klarna app, at no extra cost to browse. Getting started takes three steps:


-


Find eligible items. Open your Klarna purchase history and see which items are eligible for Care & Repair.


-


Choose a service. Select the type of care you need — such as alterations, cleaning, or repair.


-


Get matched with a trusted supplier. Save Your Wardrobe matches you with the best available specialist for the job, from booking through to completion.


**Methodology**


Research referenced in this release is drawn from a nationally representative consumer survey on repair culture and behaviour, commissioned by Klarna and Save Your Wardrobe among UK consumers (n=1,004) in August 2026.


*Saving figure based on Save Your Wardrobe repair data across UK and French partner brands. On average, customers pay 37% of an item's estimated value to repair or alter it rather than replace it — an average saving of ~£113 per customer. Item values are estimated from brands' RRP; total customer cost includes the repair, shipping and any brand markups, and varies by brand.


Annual household saving is calculated by multiplying this average per-repair saving (~£113) by the average number of items repaired per year (1.4, per Klarna's UK consumer research) and the average UK household size (2.35 people, per ONS, "Families and households in the UK: 2024").


**About Save Your Wardrobe**


Save Your Wardrobe (SYW) is an award-winning aftersales platform powering the next generation of post-purchase infrastructure for global brands and retailers. By unifying every service touchpoint into one tech-enabled ecosystem, from maintenance and care to defect management, warranty flows, and extended-life services — SYW transforms traditionally manual operations into automated, data-rich workflows that scale operational excellence and elevate the customer experience worldwide. Our mission is to help brands map, design, and automate their aftersales operations through intelligent, connected infrastructure. For more information: www.saveyourwardrobe.com


**About Klarna**


Klarna is the everyday finance network. With over 120 million global active Klarna users and 3.8 million transactions per day, Klarna's AI-powered payments and commerce network is empowering people to pay smarter with a mission to be available everywhere for everything. Consumers can pay with Klarna online, in-store and through Apple Pay & Google Pay. Over 1.2 million retailers trust Klarna's innovative solutions to drive growth and loyalty, including Uber, H&M, Saks, Sephora, Macy's, Ikea, Expedia Group, Nike and Airbnb. Klarna is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: KLAR).


The company became the first to join The Climate Pledge and Race to Zero campaign, and makes annual financial contributions to high-impact climate projects, including carbon removal, reforestation and forest protection, and emission reduction projects.


For more information, visit Klarna.com.
